health_coverage: One government health plan should cover everyone, with little or no role for private insurance.
Everyone should be able to choose between a government plan and private insurance.
Most people should keep private insurance, with government programs for older people, low-income people and those who can't get covered otherwise, roughly as today.
Most people should have private insurance, with smaller government health programs than today.
People should buy private insurance or pay directly; the government shouldn't provide coverage.
coverage_guarantee: The federal government should make sure every American is covered, through one government plan.
The federal government should make sure every American is covered, through whatever mix of public and private plans works.
The government shouldn't guarantee coverage for everyone, but should help low-income and seriously ill people get covered.
Getting health coverage is each person's own responsibility, not the government's.
medicare_age: Everyone of any age should be enrolled in Medicare automatically.
Anyone of any age should be able to choose to buy into Medicare.
Medicare should open at 60 instead of 65.
Medicare should stay at 65 and older.
The Medicare age should rise gradually to 67.
private_insurance_role: With a government plan for everyone, private insurance should only cover extras the plan doesn't, like private rooms.
Private insurers should compete with the government plan, and people choose either one.
Private insurance should stay the main system, with the government plan only for people who can't get private coverage.
drug_prices: The government should set the prices of all brand-name drugs, for everyone.
The government should negotiate prices on many more drugs, for Medicare and private insurance alike.
Medicare should keep negotiating prices on a limited number of drugs, as it does now.
The government should stop negotiating drug prices and let competition set them.
drug_import: People should be able to buy prescription drugs from any country with safety standards like ours.
Imported drugs should be allowed only through limited state programs the FDA approves.
Prescription drugs shouldn't be imported, because it's too hard to keep them safe.
medicaid_scope: Medicaid should cover all low-income adults in every state, with federal money paying most of the cost.
Medicaid should stay as it is, with each state choosing whether to cover all low-income adults.
Federal Medicaid money should be capped per person, and states should get more say over who's covered.
Each state should get a fixed amount of Medicaid money and decide everything about the program.
medicaid_work: Adults on Medicaid shouldn't have to work, volunteer or go to school to keep their coverage.
Able-bodied adults on Medicaid should have to work, volunteer or study about 80 hours a month, with exemptions for parents, caregivers and students.
Adults on Medicaid should face a stricter requirement than 80 hours a month, or fewer exemptions.
ss_shortfall: Social Security's gap should be closed only with tax increases, mainly on high earners, keeping or raising benefits.
Social Security's gap should be closed mostly with tax increases and small benefit changes.
Social Security's gap should be closed with about equal tax increases and benefit cuts.
Social Security's gap should be closed mostly by slowing benefit growth, such as raising the retirement age, with small tax increases.
Social Security's gap should be closed only by slowing benefit growth, with no tax increases.
ss_retirement_age: The full retirement age should drop to 65 for people now under 50.
The full retirement age should stay at 67.
The full retirement age should rise to 68 or 69 for people now under 50.
The full retirement age should rise to 70 or higher for people now under 50.
ss_payroll_cap: Social Security tax should apply to all wages, with no cap.
Social Security tax should also apply to wages above $400,000, leaving wages between today's cap and $400,000 untaxed.
The cap on wages subject to Social Security tax should be raised somewhat, but not removed.
The cap on wages subject to Social Security tax should stay where it is.
The Social Security tax rate should go down, even if future benefits have to shrink.
medicare_structure: Medicare should also cover dental, vision and hearing, paid for with higher taxes.
Medicare should stay as it is, with new taxes or savings to keep paying for it.
Future retirees should get a set amount to spend on either traditional Medicare or a private plan.
Medicare should be gradually replaced with personal health savings accounts.
medicare_means_test: Higher-income retirees should pay much more for Medicare than they do today.
Higher-income retirees should pay somewhat more for Medicare than they do today.
Higher-income retirees should keep paying what they pay today.
Everyone should pay the same for Medicare, whatever their income.
ss_private_accounts: Social Security should stay a guaranteed benefit, with no personal investment accounts.
Workers could have personal investment accounts only as an extra on top of Social Security, not carved out of it.
Workers should be able to choose to put part of their Social Security tax into an account they own and invest.
Social Security should gradually be replaced with personal investment accounts.
insurance_mandate: Everyone should be required to have health insurance, with a penalty for going without.
No one should be penalized, but anyone without insurance should be signed up automatically for a free basic plan.
Whether to have health insurance should be each person's own choice.
preexisting_conditions: Insurers should never be able to charge more or refuse coverage because of past health problems, as today.
Insurers can charge somewhat more for past health problems, but can't refuse to cover anyone.
Insurers can charge more or refuse coverage for past health problems, with a separate government-funded plan for people they turn down.
school_vaccines: Children should need vaccines like measles and polio to attend any school, public or private.
Children should need these vaccines to attend public schools, but private schools can set their own rules.
These vaccines should be recommended, but parents decide, even for public school.
vaccine_exemptions: These children should still need the required vaccines: {case}.
These children should be allowed to skip the required vaccines: {case}.
outbreak_gov_mandate: During a serious outbreak, the government should require most workers to get vaccinated.
During a serious outbreak, the government should require vaccines only for health care and other close-contact jobs.
The government shouldn't require anyone to get vaccinated for their job, even during a serious outbreak.
outbreak_employer: During a serious outbreak, any employer should be allowed to require its workers to get vaccinated.
During a serious outbreak, only health care employers should be allowed to require vaccines.
No employer should be allowed to require workers to get vaccinated.
immigrant_health_benefits: Anyone living here with a low enough income should be able to get Medicaid, whatever their legal status.
Legal immigrants should qualify for Medicaid right away, and children should qualify whatever their status.
Most legal immigrants should wait 5 years for Medicaid, as today, and people without legal status shouldn't qualify.
Legal immigrants should wait 10 years or more for Medicaid.
Only US citizens should be able to get Medicaid.
water_fluoride: Cities should add fluoride to drinking water, as health agencies recommend.
Each city should decide whether to add fluoride.
Adding fluoride to drinking water should be banned.
food_additives: Additives that other countries ban, like some artificial dyes, should be banned in the US too, even if US regulators approved them.
Those additives should be allowed but carry clear warning labels.
If US regulators approved an additive, it should be allowed, whatever other countries do.
long_term_care: A new government insurance program should pay for nursing home and home care for everyone.
Government should help middle-income families pay for long-term care too, not only the poor.
Keep today's system, where Medicaid pays only after people spend down their savings.
Families and private insurance should pay for long-term care, with less government help than today.
